description: A tropical cyclone is approaching a coastal district in India. Track the warning stages, prepare an emergency kit, and evacuate coastal areas before landfall.
objectives: Interpret cyclone warning stages issued by IMD-style bulletins
Prepare an emergency kit and secure your home
Evacuate low-lying coastal areas before landfall
Stay safe from wind and storm-surge hazards after landfall

steps.title: Cyclone Alert
steps.narrative: A cyclone alert (72 hours' notice) is issued for the coast near you. What should you do?

options.text: Start preparing: charge devices, secure loose outdoor items, and prepare an emergency kit
Wait for the storm to get closer before doing anything
options.mistake: Early preparation during the alert stage saves critical time — supplies and transport get harder to arrange later.

steps.title: Cyclone Warning
steps.narrative: The alert is upgraded to a cyclone warning (24 hours' notice). You live in a low-lying coastal zone.

options.text: Plan your evacuation to a designated cyclone shelter or safe relative's house inland
Decide to stay and 'wait it out' at home near the coast
options.mistake: Low-lying coastal homes are highly vulnerable to storm surge — evacuation is strongly advised at this stage.

steps.title: Final Evacuation Order
steps.narrative: Local authorities issue a mandatory evacuation order as landfall nears.

options.text: Evacuate immediately with your emergency kit and important documents
Delay to secure a few more household items first
options.mistake: Delaying a mandatory evacuation risks being caught by storm surge or high winds before reaching safety.

steps.title: At the Shelter
steps.narrative: You reach a cyclone shelter. It's crowded and a family with small children arrives after you.

options.text: Help make room and assist shelter staff where you can
Keep to your space and ignore the situation
options.mistake: Cooperating and assisting vulnerable arrivals is part of safe, effective shelter behavior.

steps.title: During Landfall
steps.narrative: The cyclone makes landfall. Winds are extremely strong outside the shelter.

options.text: Stay inside the shelter, away from windows and doors, until officials say it's safe
Step outside briefly during a lull to check conditions
options.mistake: The calm 'eye' of a cyclone is temporary — dangerous winds return quickly from the opposite direction.

steps.title: After the Storm
steps.narrative: Winds have died down and officials say the storm has moved on. Roads have flooding and debris.

options.text: Wait for an official all-clear, then return home carefully avoiding flooded and debris-covered roads
Head home right away through whatever route is fastest
options.mistake: Post-cyclone roads can have hidden hazards like downed lines, flooding, and structural debris.
